citation.title: Rhythmic coordination and ensemble dynamics in the hippocampal-prefrontal network during odor-place associative memory and decision making

extraction.method: Exact numerators and denominators transcribed from the published caption
extraction.reported_statement: CA1 spatial-field prevalence in odor-period inactive and active cells

prespecification.empirical_cue_measure: Significant CA1 activity during the odor-sampling period
prespecification.empirical_spatial_measure: Presence of a spatial firing field during maze running
prespecification.model_cue_measure: Training-lap cue main effect passing BH-FDR and partial eta-squared >= 0.05
prespecification.primary_metric: Absolute difference between empirical and aligned-model log odds ratios
secondary_metrics: Spatial prevalence conditional on cue status
prespecification.selection_rationale: The paper reports an exact CA1 population contingency between sensory-cue responsiveness and spatial coding, matching the two factors manipulated independently in E3/E6.
prespecification.unit_of_model_inference: Network/data seed after pooling the two prespecified cue layouts
prespecification.zero_cell_rule: Add 0.5 to all four contingency cells for odds-ratio estimation; report undefined when either cue group or spatial outcome is entirely absent

limitations: The empirical task uses odors to guide choices on a T-maze, whereas the model uses two sensory patterns crossed with four positions on a linear track.
The empirical variables are spike-based significance and place-field criteria; the model uses sparse binary-like activity and factorial effect criteria.
The comparison tests the population association direction and magnitude, not neuron-by-neuron correspondence or an EC3 manipulation.
